questions.q: Rubidium is below potassium in Group I. Which prediction about rubidium is correct?
options: higher melting point than potassium; reacts more slowly with water
lower melting point than potassium; reacts more vigorously with water
lower density than potassium; does not react with water
higher melting point than potassium; reacts more vigorously with water
questions.why: Down Group I melting point decreases and reactivity with water increases.
A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one: Br₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Br⁻ + I₂ (brown solution).

questions.q: Which property is typical of transition elements?
questions.why: Transition elements have high densities and melting points, form coloured compounds and often act as catalysts.

questions.q: Explain, in terms of electronic configuration, why the noble gases are unreactive.
questions.model: They have a full outer shell of electrons (a stable electronic configuration), so they do not need to lose, gain or share electrons.
points: do not lose, gain or share electrons
